title: Atypical parkinsonian syndromes

steps.tx: **Progressive supranuclear palsy** features early unexplained backward falls, symmetric axial rigidity, retrocollis, and vertical **supranuclear gaze** palsy affecting downgaze first. Supranuclear vertical gaze restriction characteristically begins with slowing of voluntary downward saccades before progressing to complete ophthalmoplegia in neurodegenerative cohorts.
steps.say: Progressive supranuclear palsy features early unexplained backward falls symmetric axial rigidity retrocollis and vertical supranuclear gaze palsy affecting downgaze first. Supranuclear vertical gaze restriction characteristically begins with slowing of voluntary downward saccades before progressing to complete ophthalmoplegia.

left.title: PSP Clinical Hallmarks
points: Early backward postural instability and falls

right.title: Parkinson Disease Comparison
points: Preserved early vertical saccadic eye movements

steps.tx: Prominent **midbrain atrophy** in progressive supranuclear palsy produces the characteristic **hummingbird sign** or penguin silhouette sign on midsagittal MRI and the Mickey Mouse sign on axial midbrain sections. Selective midbrain tegmental atrophy with preservation of the pontine base creates this distinctive morphological appearance.
steps.say: Prominent midbrain atrophy in progressive supranuclear palsy produces the characteristic hummingbird sign or penguin silhouette sign on midsagittal MRI and the Mickey Mouse sign on axial midbrain sections. Selective midbrain tegmental atrophy with preservation of the pontine base creates this distinctive morphological appearance.

steps.tx: **Multiple system atrophy** is an aggressive alpha-synucleinopathy presenting with severe **autonomic failure** such as orthostatic hypotension and neurogenic bladder, combined with either parkinsonism (MSA-P) or cerebellar ataxia (MSA-C). Histological detection of silver-staining glial cytoplasmic inclusions within oligodendrocytes confirms definitive neuropathological diagnosis.
steps.say: Multiple system atrophy is an aggressive alpha-synucleinopathy presenting with severe autonomic failure such as orthostatic hypotension and neurogenic bladder combined with either parkinsonism MSA-P or cerebellar ataxia MSA-C. Histological detection of silver-staining glial cytoplasmic inclusions within oligodendrocytes confirms definitive neuropathological diagnosis.

rows: Putaminal slit sign and rim hypointensity on T2
Gait and limb ataxia, intention tremor, dysarthria
Hot cross bun sign and cerebellar atrophy

steps.tx: Brain magnetic resonance imaging in MSA-C characteristically demonstrates the **hot cross bun sign** on T2-weighted axial images, representing selective degeneration of **pontocerebellar** transverse fibres and raphe nuclei with preservation of the descending corticospinal tracts within the basis pontis on structural neuroimaging.
steps.say: Brain magnetic resonance imaging in MSA-C characteristically demonstrates the hot cross bun sign on T2-weighted axial images representing selective degeneration of pontocerebellar transverse fibres and raphe nuclei with preservation of the descending corticospinal tracts within the basis pontis on structural neuroimaging.

left.title: Neuropathological Basis
points: Neuronal loss in pontine raphe nuclei
Cruciform T2 hyperintensity in pontine basis

right.title: Spared Structures
points: Cruciform pattern created by spared tissue margins

steps.tx: Severe autonomic failure in multiple system atrophy presents with profound orthostatic hypotension, defined by a blood pressure drop of at least **30** mmHg systolic or **15** mmHg diastolic within **3** minutes of standing, accompanied by urinary incontinence or retention and nocturnal laryngeal stridor.
steps.say: Severe autonomic failure in multiple system atrophy presents with profound orthostatic hypotension defined by a blood pressure drop of at least 30 mmHg systolic or 15 mmHg diastolic within 3 minutes of standing accompanied by urinary incontinence or retention and nocturnal laryngeal stridor.

left.title: Cardiovascular Autonomic Failure
points: Systolic drop >=30 mmHg or diastolic >=15 mmHg
Absence of compensatory heart rate acceleration

right.title: Urogenital and Respiratory Failure
points: Urinary urge incontinence and large post-void residual
Erectile dysfunction as an early sentinel symptom
Nocturnal laryngeal stridor requiring urgent CPAP
Vocal cord abductor paralysis on laryngoscopy

steps.tx: **Corticobasal** syndrome is a 4R-tauopathy featuring asymmetric progressive limb dystonia, limb apraxia, cortical sensory loss (astereognosis, agraphesthesia), myoclonus, and the pathognomonic **alien limb** phenomenon where the affected limb displays autonomous involuntary motor behaviors outside volitional control during spontaneous daily motor activities.
steps.say: Corticobasal syndrome is a 4R-tauopathy featuring asymmetric progressive limb dystonia limb apraxia cortical sensory loss astereognosis agraphesthesia myoclonus and the pathognomonic alien limb phenomenon where the affected limb displays autonomous involuntary motor behaviors outside volitional control.

left.title: Cortical Manifestations
points: Alien limb phenomenon and motor neglect
Ideomotor limb apraxia refractory to cues
Focal myoclonus stimulated by tactile action

right.title: Extrapyramidal Manifestations
points: Complete lack of sustained levodopa response

steps.tx: **Dementia with Lewy bodies** features the clinical tetrad of fluctuating cognition with pronounced variations in attention and alertness, recurrent well-formed **visual hallucinations**, spontaneous parkinsonism, and REM sleep behavior disorder. Patients exhibit severe life-threatening neuroleptic sensitivity when exposed to typical first-generation antipsychotics.
steps.say: Dementia with Lewy bodies features the clinical tetrad of fluctuating cognition with pronounced variations in attention and alertness recurrent well-formed visual hallucinations spontaneous parkinsonism and REM sleep behavior disorder. Patients exhibit severe life-threatening neuroleptic sensitivity when exposed to typical first-generation antipsychotics.

rows: Spontaneous alterations in attention and alertness
Symmetric bradykinesia and rigidity without tremor
Modest and transient response to levodopa
Loss of REM motor atonia with dream enactment
Melatonin or clonazepam for nighttime safety

steps.tx: Pathologically, progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration are four-repeat (4R) **tauopathies** with tufted astrocytes and astrocytic plaques respectively, whereas multiple system atrophy and dementia with Lewy bodies are alpha-synucleinopathies with **glial cytoplasmic inclusions** within central oligodendrocytes throughout affected subcortical tracts.
steps.say: Pathologically progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration are four-repeat 4R tauopathies with tufted astrocytes and astrocytic plaques respectively whereas multiple system atrophy and dementia with Lewy bodies are alpha-synucleinopathies with glial cytoplasmic inclusions within oligodendrocytes.
